kamishibai agent contract
Release: 1.8.0

Overview

kamishibai turns a list of words into an illustrated Anki deck using Google
Gemini. Each card has a native example sentence, native-speaker audio, and a
manga panel.

This file describes the headless console contract for agents and scripts.
Running `kamishibai` with no arguments opens the interactive TUI, which is out
of scope here.

First-time headless setup

Run this before relying on a remote document:

```bash
kamishibai agent-contract
```

It prints the contract embedded in the installed binary. Its `Release` always
matches that binary's application version. The release-pinned remote copy is
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/anatoly-chichikov/kamishibai/v1.8.0/llms.txt`;
never use mutable `main/llms.txt` as the installed binary's contract.

Language terminology is fixed:

```text
known = my = source
learning = target
```

Only `known` is saved globally. `learning` belongs to a session: pass it
explicitly or let word intake autodetect it. Do not create or edit
`preferences.json` by hand; `config` owns that file.

For CI, shared, remote, or ephemeral agents, keep the key in the environment
or a secret manager and pass it to every command that calls Gemini:

```bash
kamishibai config --json
GEMINI_API_KEY="$SECRET" \
  kamishibai new --word chat --known RU --learning FR --json
GEMINI_API_KEY="$SECRET" kamishibai generate --json
```

The detached worker inherits the environment of `generate`. A later
`regenerate` or `correct` invocation needs the environment key again.

For a personal single-user installation, save the known language and a
verified key once:

```bash
kamishibai config --known RU --json
printf '%s' "$GEMINI_API_KEY" |
  kamishibai config --key - --json
kamishibai config --json
```

`--key -` keeps the key out of argv and shell history. Literal
`--key VALUE` remains supported, but can expose the value through both.
`GEMINI_API_KEY` always wins over a saved key. `config` with no flags is
offline and shows only redacted setup state; it never prints the key.

Process model

Each command is one process call that runs to completion and exits. There is no
daemon, socket, or open stream. Drive the flow by calling commands in sequence.

Use `--json` after the verb on every agent call except `agent-contract`, which
is the text contract itself. Plain text is for humans, has no stable shape, and
prints nothing bare to capture.

A session is the persistent unit of work. It is created by `new` and stored on
disk. It holds the words, proposed senses, curation choices, committed plan,
worker state, and result. Create one session per batch of words and reuse it.
Do not call `new` again to re-read or rebuild the same batch; use `status`,
`result`, `adjust`, or `regenerate`.

Every stateful verb takes an optional `<id>`, but a single-batch workflow usually
omits it. kamishibai resolves a lone session, or the lone unfinished one,
automatically. If several sessions match, the command refuses with exit code 5
and lists candidates in `sessions`; pass an id only then. Read `session` from
any JSON document when you do need the id.

`generate`, `regenerate`, and `new --generate` start a detached background worker
by default and return immediately with `phase` set to `generating`. Poll
`status --json` every few seconds until `phase` becomes terminal. Do not
tight-loop. Pass `--wait` to keep the process open until the worker finishes;
with `--wait`, progress events are streamed as NDJSON on stderr.

`new` and `correct` call Gemini too, but they finish before returning.

Session lifecycle

understood -> curate -> generating -> terminal

Terminal phases are:

- `published`: every card made the deck
- `partial`: some cards failed, and the deck contains the rest
- `failed`: no card survived
- `interrupted`: a worker died
- `cancelled`: a worker was stopped

Generation is cache-backed and idempotent. A killed, interrupted, or partial run
resumes and fills only what is missing, so re-running `generate` is cheap and
safe.

Invocation

Place `--json` after the verb:

```bash
kamishibai status --json
kamishibai result --json
```

Putting `--json` before the verb is a parse error.

stdout in JSON mode is exactly one JSON document per call: either the success
document or the error envelope. Nothing else is written to stdout.

stderr carries human narration, lower-layer noise such as model downloads, and
the NDJSON event stream for `generate --wait` or `regenerate --wait`. Ignore
stderr lines that do not parse as JSON; stderr is not strict.

Error envelope

```json
{
  "ok": false,
  "error": {
    "code": "usage|not_found|not_ready|ambiguous|operational",
    "exit": 2,
    "message": "...",
    "hint": "run: kamishibai config --known EN --json",
    "retryable": false
  }
}
```

`retryable` is always present. `hint` is present when kamishibai has a concrete
next action; it is omitted when no safe generic action exists. The
ambiguous-session envelope also carries a top-level `sessions` array with the
newest five candidates, using the same shape as an `ls` item.

Exit codes

- `0`: ok
- `2`: usage error; the invocation, state, or config is wrong
- `3`: no such session
- `4`: not ready yet; retry after state changes, such as `result` before publish
- `5`: ambiguous session; an omitted id matched several sessions
- `1`: other operational error

Branch on the exit code first, then read `retryable`. A timeout, DNS failure,
HTTP 429, HTTP 408, or HTTP 5xx is an operational exit 1 with
`retryable: true`; an invalid key is usage exit 2 with `retryable: false`.
Codes, locking, idempotency, and session semantics are identical with and
without `--json`; `--json` changes only the representation.

All language codes are uppercase in every document, id, cache path, and deck
filename: `EN`, `FR`, `JA`, and so on. Input accepts any case and is normalized.

Future CLI JSON documents are additive: keys may be added, but existing keys are
not renamed or removed.

Commands

Per-verb flags and signatures: run `kamishibai <verb> --help`.

`agent-contract`

Prints the exact contract embedded in the installed binary, including its
matching application version in `Release`. It is text-only and refuses
`--json` with exit 2.

`new`

```text
kamishibai new (--word W [--word W...] | --words FILE | --build FILE)
  [--known L] [--learning L] [--senses primary|all]
  [--level a1|a2|b1|b2|c1|c2]
  [--types best-fit|statements|questions|dialogue|mixed]
  [--id NAME] [--out DIR] [--generate [--wait]]
```

Word intake completes Gemini understanding before creating an `understood`
session; a cards JSON import skips understanding and takes its language pair
from the entries. An explicit `--learning` value is normalized and validated
before credential lookup, Gemini, cache writes, or session creation. It
constrains Gemini understanding to that target and must match Gemini's returned
target. Every explicit target and autodetection use separate understanding-cache
identities. `--known` falls back to saved config; without either value, the
command refuses and points to `config --known`.

`--level` pins one lowercase operational CEFR band for the surrounding
language on every card. Without it, metadata writes the natural example first
and attributes its honest level afterward. `--types best-fit` leaves each
example format unconstrained and is the default. `statements`, `questions`,
and `dialogue` pin that exact format on every selected card. `mixed`
deterministically gives each complete group of five cards three statements,
one question, and one dialogue; it never assigns requests or exclamations.
The allocation is stable across retries and process restarts. The retired
`natural` and `varied` values remain accepted as aliases for `best-fit` and
`mixed`.

These settings are initial metadata constraints, not a second rewrite pass:
each card still makes at most the ordinary one metadata request per attempt.
When neither a level nor a non-`best-fit` type policy is requested, the rendered metadata
prompt and provider-call shape are unchanged. This release advances the
metadata policy, so a card carrying metadata from an older policy refreshes it
once even under defaults. Explicit settings are accepted with both word intake
and `--build`; an imported card whose cached metadata does not satisfy them is
refreshed only when generation starts.

`--generate` immediately commits and starts the session. Add `--wait` to run
that generation in the same foreground process; `--wait` without `--generate`
is a usage error.

`select`

Selection re-includes a previously excluded card and resets the session to
`understood`.

`exclude`

The excluded card stays visible in the understanding, and the session resets to
`understood`.

`correct`

Calls Gemini synchronously to add senses, then resets the session to
`understood`.

`generate`

Commits the curated plan. Detached generation returns immediately with `phase`
set to `generating`; poll `status`. Waiting blocks until terminal state, streams
NDJSON events on stderr, and returns the terminal document. If every card fails,
it exits 1 with the error envelope; if nothing is selected, it exits 2. A
session carrying staged sentence adjustments refuses before spawning a worker;
activate the whole pending batch with `regenerate --pending`.

By default, fresh card metadata first writes the natural sentence required by
the approved understanding and only then assigns its descriptive register,
phrase kind, and lowercase `a1`–`c2` level. Initial generation targets a band or
phrase kind only when `new --level` or a non-`best-fit` `new --types` requested it. When
an exact requested value would make the accepted use unnatural, the closest
natural result keeps its actual attribution and records the requested target
separately. That pinned axis is also named in `approx`; this is a best-effort
outcome, not a failed card.

`status`

Reads only the cache and never calls Gemini. Before a plan is committed, the
session document contains candidates; after commit, it contains per-card
artifact state.

`adjust`

Stages one committed card's sentence rewrite without calling Gemini, deleting
artifacts, starting a worker, or changing the session phase or published
result. Its grammar is:

```text
kamishibai adjust [<id>] --card TERM [--understanding TEXT]
  [--register neutral|casual|formal|literary|archaic]
  [--kind statement|question|request|exclamation|dialogue]
  [--level a1|a2|b1|b2|c1|c2]
  [--restore register|level|kind|all] [--note TEXT]
```

At least one of `--register`, `--kind`, `--level`, `--restore`, or `--note`
is required. `--restore` is repeatable and comma-delimited: both
`--restore register --restore level` and `--restore register,level` are valid.
`all` means all three label axes. Restoring an axis copies that axis from the
card's current baseline, including its pin and approximation state; on legacy
metadata without labels it restores the axis to unknown. Restore never changes
the note. If a value and `--restore` name the same axis in one call, the
explicit value is applied after the restore and wins.

Every flag is a patch. An omitted axis or note preserves the card's already
staged value. An explicitly empty `--note ''` clears the note. If all three
axes equal the current baseline and the note is blank, the card has no pending
adjustment. Repeated calls may accumulate adjustments on several cards before
one generation run.

`--card` must identify exactly one committed card. It is enough when the term
is unique. If selected senses produced several cards with the same term, add
the exact `understanding` shown by `status` as `--understanding TEXT`; an
ambiguous term is refused rather than silently selecting the first card.

An imported `new --build` card can have current metadata without sentence
labels. Adjusting such a card is supported: its pending selection contains only
the explicitly chosen axes, and the first successful rewrite attributes the
other axes. `adjust` is offline and never requires a Gemini key.

`open`

Resumes the session in the interactive TUI. It is not for agents and refuses
`--json` with exit 2.

`result`

Ready when `phase` is `published` or `partial`; otherwise exits 4. Returns a
result document with deck paths and full per-card data that round-trips through
cards JSON.

`regenerate`

Takes exactly one target: `--failed`, `--card T`, or `--pending`. `--failed`
retries incomplete cards from their first missing stages. `--card` fully
re-rolls one committed card and may carry `--note "..."` for an immediate
rewrite. Both rebuild and republish through the same worker as `generate`.

`--pending` atomically activates every adjustment staged by `adjust` or the
interactive editor, then starts one worker. It is the headless equivalent of
`Ctrl+G`: several cards remain pending until this command, and all start
together. A detached call returns with `phase: "generating"`; `--wait` streams
the ordinary generation events and returns the terminal session document. On a
partial session, the same run also resumes other missing artifact stages before
republishing; it never discards a valid artifact from an untouched card.
`generate`, `regenerate --failed`, and `regenerate --card` refuse while staged
adjustments exist, before provider work or cache invalidation, and point to
`regenerate --pending`.

Every full-card rewrite carries the complete current sentence-label preset.
Every unedited axis keeps its current requested target. Only an explicitly
changed or already pinned axis may differ from that target, and the response
must name the axis in `approx`. Such a result is accepted as the closest natural
sentence: `labels` reports the actual attribution and `labels.requested` keeps
the target. With a rewrite note, Gemini also applies the note while rewriting
that card. A successful rewrite replaces `labels` and removes `adjustment`; an
interrupted or failed rewrite keeps an active adjustment so a later `generate`
can resume it.

`cancel`

Stops the running worker but preserves cached artifacts for a later resume. It
always exits 0 with the correct final phase, even when racing a finishing
worker; gate on `phase`, not `ok`.

`ls`

Returns `{"ok": true, "sessions": []}` with an item for every session.

`rm`

Returns `{"ok": true, "removed": "<id>"}` after deletion.

`cache-path`

Returns `{"ok": true, "cache": "/..."}` with the resolved cache directory.

`config`

The known language is validated against the catalog and saved uppercase. A key
is verified through the authenticated model-list endpoint with a short timeout,
including `generateContent` support, without generating content. It is saved
only after a successful probe and is never printed back.

The result contains `ok: true`, `known`, `key_saved`, `credential_source`,
`credential_present`, and `preferences_path`. `credential_source` is
`environment`, `saved`, or `none`, with environment winning. Presence means a
non-empty key is available, not that a network check ran; `key_saved` reports
the fallback even when environment wins. `known` is always present and is
`null` until saved.

JSON documents

Session document

Returned by `new`, `select`, `exclude`, `correct`, `adjust`, `generate`,
`regenerate`, `cancel`, and `status`. Mutating verbs return the post-mutation
state, so no follow-up `status` call is required.

Presence rules:

- `phase` is always present and is one of `understood`, `generating`,
  `published`, `partial`, `failed`, `interrupted`, or `cancelled`
- `candidates` is present whenever curatable senses exist
- `cards` is present once a plan is committed
- `candidates` and `cards` can appear together during and after generation
- `worker`, `progress`, `result`, and `error` appear only when present
- absent fields are omitted, never null
- `sentences` is always present; `types` is `best-fit`, `statements`,
  `questions`, `dialogue`, or `mixed`, while
  `level` is omitted when the batch did not request one
- `progress` appears only while generating
- a sense's 1-based position in its `senses` array is its `select --sense`
  number
- a card's state is derived from artifacts in order: `meta`, `sound`, `scene`,
  then `picture`
- all four artifacts set to `true` means the card is in the deck
- the first false artifact is where the card stands or failed
- `cards.pending` is always present after commit and counts staged, not active,
  adjustments
- `labels` is the card's current complete attribution and is omitted only when
  current metadata has no labels
- `labels.requested` is present when one or more axes were pinned; its values
  are the targets that generation or regeneration aimed for, while the sibling
  `register`, `kind`, and `level` remain the actual attribution of the generated
  sentence
- `adjustment` is present while a rewrite is staged or active; `state` is
  `pending` before `regenerate --pending` and `active` after activation
- `adjustment.labels` is a selection: `register`, `kind`, and `level` are each
  omitted when a legacy baseline has not attributed that axis; `pinned` and
  `approx` are always arrays
- `adjustment.note` is present only when non-empty
- `approx` is always a subset of `pinned`; an axis in `approx` may have different
  actual and requested values without failing the card; all tokens and axes are
  lowercase

Example:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "session": "FR-20260614_091500_ab3x",
  "created": "2026-06-14T09:15:00Z",
  "pair": {"known": "EN", "learning": "FR"},
  "senses": "primary",
  "sentences": {"level": "b1", "types": "questions"},
  "source": "words",
  "out": "/abs/out",
  "phase": "published",
  "candidates": {
    "items": [
      {
        "term": "canard",
        "included": true,
        "senses": [
          {"tag": "zool.", "understanding": "a duck", "selected": true},
          {"understanding": "a hoax", "selected": false}
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "result": {
    "deck": "/abs/out/FR.apkg",
    "pdf": "/abs/out/FR.pdf",
    "dir": "/abs/out"
  },
  "cards": {
    "pending": 1,
    "items": [
      {
        "term": "canard",
        "understanding": "a duck",
        "artifacts": {
          "meta": true,
          "sound": true,
          "scene": true,
          "picture": true
        },
        "labels": {
          "register": "neutral",
          "kind": "question",
          "level": "b1",
          "pinned": ["level", "kind"],
          "approx": [],
          "requested": {
            "kind": "question",
            "level": "b1"
          }
        },
        "adjustment": {
          "state": "pending",
          "labels": {
            "register": "neutral",
            "kind": "question",
            "level": "b2",
            "pinned": ["level", "kind"],
            "approx": []
          }
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Result document

Returned by `result`. `items` are strict cards JSON entries, the exact
`new --build` schema with uppercase `lang`, so they round-trip into a new
session. The top-level `sentences` object repeats the batch setting that
produced the result even though the strict card entries do not carry that
session provenance.

Example:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "session": "FR-20260614_091500_ab3x",
  "pair": {"known": "EN", "learning": "FR"},
  "sentences": {"level": "b1", "types": "questions"},
  "phase": "published",
  "paths": {"deck": "/o/FR.apkg", "pdf": "/o/FR.pdf", "dir": "/o"},
  "failed": 0,
  "items": ["...strict cards JSON entries..."]
}
```

`ls` item

Used in `ls` and in ambiguous-session error envelopes.

Example:

```json
{
  "id": "FR-20260614_091500_ab3x",
  "pair": {"known": "EN", "learning": "FR"},
  "created": "2026-06-14T09:15:00Z",
  "phase": "published",
  "cards": {"total": 2, "ready": 2}
}
```

Before a plan is committed, the item carries `selected` instead of `cards`.

Wait events

`generate --wait` and `regenerate --wait` emit NDJSON lines on stderr. The final
session document still goes to stdout. `retry` and `retries` appear only on
retry or failure, and so do `category` and `reason`, which name why the try that
just failed was spent.

Examples:

```json
{"event": "generating", "cards": 2}
{"event": "step", "term": "canard", "artifact": "picture", "status": "retry", "retry": 1, "retries": 3, "category": "border", "reason": "White border missing on: bottom"}
{"event": "step", "term": "canard", "artifact": "picture", "status": "ok"}
{"event": "publishing"}
{"event": "warning", "message": "..."}
```

Step status is one of `ok`, `cache`, `retry`, or `fail`. Artifact is one of
`meta`, `sound`, `scene`, or `picture`.

Every artifact gets one plain try plus `retries` (3) retries on top of it, so at
most four artifact attempts. One picture attempt may contain the image request,
its literal-writing gate (OCR or Gemini), the full-frame recall request that
independently checks answer leakage, scene fidelity, and literal policy, a final
card-free dedicated scene-fidelity request, a scale-aware literal-writing zoom
request, and an adaptive full-frame
judge-recovery call when structured output reaches its token ceiling.
The first try is never numbered: `retry` counts the retry the reported failure
has just triggered, from `1` to `retries`. A `fail` step means all retries were
spent and carries `retries` without `retry`.

`category` is the renderer's verdict slug for a picture the model did draw and a
local gate rejected — `border`, `topology`, `color`, `ocr`, `recall_text`,
`legacy_gutter`, `other` — or `error` when infrastructure failed rather than a
gate rejecting the picture (transport, cache lease, exhausted request budget,
OCR failure, or Gemini judge failure). Every rejected picture stays on disk under
`cards/<known>-<learning>/<key>/visual/<revision>/attempts/attempt-NNNN.jpg`
next to its `attempt-NNNN.json` verdict, the `attempt-NNNN.scene.json` it was
drawn from, the `attempt-NNNN.prompt.txt` compiled for it, the
`attempt-NNNN.text.json` literal-writing verdict when that gate ran, and the
`attempt-NNNN.recall.json` merged review (independent answer-leakage,
scene-fidelity, and literal-policy verdicts plus explicit proof of dedicated
fidelity and zoom inspection) only when the picture advanced to those later
gates. A rejected frame can therefore be read against its own scene
and every gate that actually reviewed it after the run. A scene step
that fails after the model answered
archives that answer in the same folder as `scene-NNNN.json` (when the reply
parses as JSON and failed later validation) or `scene-NNNN.txt` (when it never
was JSON), so a rejected scene is readable too. Nothing in the archive is pruned
by a later run; `regenerate` is what clears it.

On `--wait`, stdout carries the final document: `phase` is `published` or
`partial`. A run where every card failed exits 1 with the error envelope, and
`status` then shows `phase` as `failed`. A cancel that raced in yields `ok: true`
with `phase: cancelled` and no result; gate on `phase`, not `ok`.

Requirements

Gemini key

Commands that call Gemini require a Gemini API key: `new --word`, `new --words`,
`correct`, `generate`, `regenerate`, and `config --key`.

Offline commands that do not need a key: `status`, `result`, `ls`, `rm`,
`cache-path`, `select`, `exclude`, `adjust`, `cancel`, and `new --build`. A
later generation for a `new --build` session still needs a key.

Set `GEMINI_API_KEY`, which wins, or save a key with `config --key -`. A saved
key means `GEMINI_API_KEY` does not need to be set. On Unix, the preferences
directory is mode 0700 and `preferences.json` is mode 0600. On Windows, writes
apply a protected owner-only ACL; a preferences file from an older release is
hardened once before its contents are returned. On shared or ephemeral systems,
use the environment instead of saving a key.

OCR models

Every structurally valid generated picture next passes the language profile's
literal-writing gate. Most languages use a typed PP-OCRv5 bundle; the first run
for one of those languages downloads its model files into the cache. `HE` and
`VI` bypass OCR entirely and use the structured Gemini Flash vision text judge
because no usable PP-OCRv5 bundle exists for those profiles. The separate
full-frame recall judge still runs afterward for every language and checks both
semantic answer leakage and whether required scene subjects, anchors, and
relations survived rendering. A clean full-frame verdict then reaches the
card-free dedicated Gemini Flash scene-fidelity judge; only a clean dedicated
verdict reaches the final enlarged-crop literal-writing judge.

Languages

- `EN`: English
- `ZH`: Chinese
- `ES`: Spanish
- `JA`: Japanese
- `FR`: French
- `DE`: German
- `KO`: Korean
- `RU`: Russian
- `IT`: Italian
- `PT`: Portuguese
- `HI`: Hindi
- `AR`: Arabic
- `TR`: Turkish
- `PL`: Polish
- `UK`: Ukrainian
- `ID`: Indonesian
- `VI`: Vietnamese
- `TH`: Thai
- `EL`: Greek
- `HE`: Hebrew
- `NL`: Dutch

Input schema for `new --build`

`new --build FILE --json` accepts a strict cards JSON document. `FILE` can be a path or
`-` for stdin. Every field is required, and unknown fields are rejected.

Rules:

- `importance` is an integer from 1 to 10
- text fields must be non-empty
- language codes must be non-empty
- language codes accept any case and are normalized to uppercase in the session

Example:

```json
{
  "entries": [
    {
      "term": "lantern",
      "meaning": "a portable lamp",
      "pronunciation": "LAN-tern",
      "transcription": "/lantern/",
      "importance": 7,
      "source": {
        "sentence": "I carried a lantern through the dark hallway.",
        "lang": "en",
        "highlight": "lantern",
        "hint": "portable light",
        "context": "a simple everyday sentence"
      },
      "target": {
        "sentence": "Ich trug eine Laterne durch den dunklen Flur.",
        "lang": "de"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

Cache and preferences

Print the cache root with `cache-path`.

Default cache locations:

- macOS: `~/Library/Caches/kamishibai`
- Linux: `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/kamishibai` or `~/.cache/kamishibai`
- Windows: the platform-native user cache directory plus `kamishibai`
- override: `KAMISHIBAI_CACHE`, interpreted as the exact cache root

Saved language and key live in `preferences.json`:

- macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/kamishibai/preferences.json`
- Linux: `${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/kamishibai/preferences.json`
- Windows: the platform-native user data directory plus
  `kamishibai/preferences.json`
- override: `KAMISHIBAI_DATA` is the data home, then
  `kamishibai/preferences.json` is appended

Output precedence for every new TUI or console session:

1. explicit `--out DIR`
2. `KAMISHIBAI_OUTPUT`, interpreted as the exact output root
3. the platform Documents directory plus `Kamishibai`
4. home plus `Kamishibai` when Documents cannot be resolved

macOS normally resolves to `~/Documents/Kamishibai`. Windows uses the native
Documents Known Folder even when the user moved it. Linux uses
`XDG_DOCUMENTS_DIR` from `user-dirs.dirs`, then `~/Documents/Kamishibai`.
If neither Documents nor home can be resolved, `new` refuses with a hint to pass
`--out` or `KAMISHIBAI_OUTPUT`.

Absolute `KAMISHIBAI_DATA`, `KAMISHIBAI_CACHE`, and `KAMISHIBAI_OUTPUT`
overrides do not require a home directory. Relative output overrides resolve
from the current working directory. Keep every runtime override identical
across calls in one workflow. A session stores its resolved absolute output
path when created, so existing sessions and old artifacts are never migrated.

Cache layout:

- `<cache>/cards/<KNOWN>-<LEARNING>/<key>/`: `meta.json`, `audio.wav`, and
  `visual/<revision>/` containing `scene.json` and `picture.jpg` for the current
  content-addressed visual policy
- `<cache>/understanding/<KNOWN>-<LEARNING>/<key>.json`
- `<cache>/sessions/<id>/`: `session.json`, `worker.log`
- `<cache>/ocr-models/`: shared OCR model files

`<key>` is a short content hash. `status` derives card readiness from the
artifact files in the current visual-policy revision and ignores older visual
directories. Deleting a card folder forces that card to regenerate on the next
`generate`. The revision hashes the embedded feature and scene-composer
prompts; the composer schema; the literal-text, full-recall, dedicated-fidelity,
and scale-aware literal-zoom judge prompt/schema pairs; the all-language recall examples; both
layout/device registries; the manga template; and a manual policy version that
changes when model configuration, local validation, or renderer acceptance
changes independently of those assets.

Script example

A single-batch workflow needs no id; omit it everywhere. Break the poll loop on
every terminal phase, not just `published`, or it spins forever on a failed run.

```bash
set -euo pipefail
GEMINI_API_KEY="$SECRET" \
  kamishibai new --word flâner --word canard --known EN --learning FR \
  --level b1 --types questions --json >/dev/null
kamishibai exclude --card canard --json >/dev/null
GEMINI_API_KEY="$SECRET" kamishibai generate --json >/dev/null
while :; do
  phase=$(kamishibai status --json | jq -r .phase)
  case "$phase" in
    published) break ;;
    partial) echo 'some cards failed; deck is partial' >&2; break ;;
    failed|interrupted|cancelled) echo 'generation did not finish' >&2; exit 1 ;;
    *) sleep 5 ;;
  esac
done
deck=$(kamishibai result --json | jq -r .paths.deck)
```
